entities.pb_arm_name: ANZ Institutional > Markets > Commodities (subsidiary ANZ Commodity Trading Pty Ltd); hubs Sydney, Singapore, Hong Kong, Shanghai, London
entities.shelf_summary: In-house bullion liquidity, not a client-wealth shelf. ANZ is an LBMA FULL member (NOT one of the 12 LBMA Market Makers - correct the premise), a Shanghai Gold Benchmark fixing bank (1 of 12), SGEI international member, PBoC-licensed gold importer via ANZ Shanghai (Dec-2013), and a CFETS interbank gold first-tier market maker (2016). Historically one of Asia's largest bullion businesses (c.15% of world primary gold production distributed in 2013; Perth Mint overseas-distribution agreement not renewed in 2016; Risk 'Asia metals dealer of the year' 2015 and Energy Risk Asia Precious Metals House of the Year under Eddie Listorti). Scaled back 2018-19 (sold physical-gold ETF JV stake 2018; closed Singapore vault Jan-2019) but FY25 shows a re-expansion: commodities trading assets A$9.08bn (+42% yoy), commodity derivative fair values doubled, commodities VaR A$8.9m as at 30-Sep-2025 vs A$3.3m. Institutional product page: swaps and options in gold, silver, platinum, palladium (options via FX Options desk) plus inventory finance, flow hedging and structured/bundled commodity finance. The '2016 precious-metals spot-fixing settlement' in the brief could NOT be verified - ANZ's 2016-17 ASIC settlement was BBSW (A$50m, Nov-2017), not metals.

strategic_idea: ANZ is a liquidity competitor, not a wealth-shelf competitor: its only client-facing metals product is the A$128m State Street Gold Fund feeder into GLDM that ANZ Private commissioned in 2024 (0.14% fee, no physical, no Lombard, no structured notes), while retail broking, Asian wealth and physical custody have all been divested (CMC 2023, DBS 2018, Singapore vault closed 2019). Three angles for a bullion desk. (1) ANZ Private white-space: with a ~A$9bn book running an explicit gold overweight, ANZ Private has no allocated-metal, delivery, gold-collateral lending or gold-linked note capability - a bullion desk could offer ANZ Private/its DIMS (or the ex-ANZ HNW clients now at CMC/DBS) allocated loco-London gold, gold-backed Lombard lines and AUD gold-linked structured notes that the SSGA fund cannot. (2) Institutional: ANZ's commodity trading assets jumped to A$9.1bn and commodity VaR nearly tripled in FY25 - the desk is rebuilding physical/consignment inventory for Asian refiner-jeweller flows using its PBoC import licence, SGE fixing seat and CFETS market-making status; ANZ is an LBMA full member (not a market maker) and now lacks its own vault, so it needs loco-London/Zurich liquidity, leasing, swaps and custody from market makers - a bullion desk (LPMCL member since Jul-2026) should be a counterparty of choice for ANZ's Asia book (location swaps London<>Shanghai/Singapore, consignment funding, Pt/Pd options which ANZ only offers via its FX options desk). (3) Product intel: the State Street/GLDM feeder shows Australian private banks will outsource gold to a US ETF rather than build accounts - a a bullion desk-custodied AUD unallocated/allocated account or feeder with delivery optionality priced near 0.14% would be a direct displacement pitch to ANZ Private, NAB/CBA/Westpac private and Australian IFAs.
